question: If a car moves 100 m in 5 seconds, its linear velocity is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**20 m/s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Linear Velocity** is defined as the rate of change of the **displacement** of an object with respect to **time**. It is a **vector quantity**, meaning it possesses both **magnitude** and **direction**.
 
• The mathematical formula for calculating velocity is **Velocity (v) = Displacement (s) / Time (t)**. In the context of a car moving in a straight line, the distance covered represents the magnitude of displacement.
 
• In this specific problem, the **displacement** is given as **100 meters** and the **time interval** is **5 seconds**. By applying the formula: **100 / 5**, we obtain a value of **20**.
 
• The **SI unit** for velocity is **meters per second (m/s)**. Therefore, the linear velocity of the car is **20 m/s**. ***Hence, the correct answer is 20 m/s.***
 
• Linear velocity differs from **angular velocity**, as the former refers to motion along a **straight path**, while the latter refers to the rate of change of **angular displacement** during circular motion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Difference between Speed and Velocity:** 
 
 
• **Speed** is a **scalar quantity** that refers to "how fast an object is moving," calculating the total **distance** covered over time.
 
• **Velocity** is a **vector quantity** that considers the **direction** of motion and uses **displacement** (the shortest distance between start and end points) instead of total distance.
 
 
 
• **Types of Velocity:**
 
 
• **Uniform Velocity:** When an object covers **equal displacements** in **equal intervals of time**, it is said to be moving with uniform velocity.
 
• **Non-uniform (Variable) Velocity:** When either the **speed** or the **direction** of an object changes over time, its velocity is considered non-uniform.
 
• **Instantaneous Velocity:** This refers to the velocity of an object at a **specific point in time** or at a specific point in its path.
 
 
 
• **Unit Conversions:** In many physics problems, velocity may be given in **kilometers per hour (km/h)**. To convert **km/h to m/s**, you multiply the value by **5/18**. Conversely, to convert **m/s to km/h**, you multiply by **18/5**. For example, **20 m/s** is equivalent to **72 km/h**.
 
• **Acceleration:** The rate at which the **velocity** of an object changes is called **acceleration**. If the car in the question was increasing its speed from 0 to 20 m/s over those 5 seconds, it would be experiencing **linear acceleration**, measured in **m/s²**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **magnitude** of velocity is equal to the **speed** only when the object moves in a **straight line** without changing direction.
 
• If an object returns to its **starting position** after moving 100 meters (e.g., moves 50m forward and 50m back), its **total displacement** would be **0**, and therefore its **average velocity** would also be **0 m/s**, despite having a non-zero average speed.
 
• In **Newton's First Law of Motion**, an object will maintain a constant **velocity** (including a velocity of zero) unless acted upon by an **external unbalanced force**.
